meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so we have twenty minutes. Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went into the gradebook?
I'm waiting, Hale. Owen found out from his phone in the middle of a class, and nobody called me. Start there.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require that the zero on Owen's essay be withdrawn, that I receive an apology, and that nothing about this is placed on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, with nothing agreed; she still wants the zero withdrawn, an apology, and nothing on Owen's record, and she was heading to the principal.
What moved her: nothing.
What cost ground: nothing, though "Thanks for coming in." skipped her direct question about who decided and whether Owen was heard, so she grew more impatient.
Try next time: when she first asks who decided and whether Owen was heard, admit in one sentence that the zero went into the gradebook before anyone called home, then show her one dated document she can check herself.
